title: Dynamic SLO-Respecting Eviction Allocator for Continuous Batches
text:
Dynamic SLO-Respecting Eviction Allocator for Continuous Batches

description:
Problem: Continuous batching improves throughput but creates long-lived GPU allocations and KV cache residency that can cause SLO violations for latency-sensitive tenants during load spikes. The current preemption heuristics are coarse (hard time-slices or blunt eviction) and either overshoot (hurting throughput/cost) or under-react (missing latency targets).

Goal: Design and implement a dynamic allocator that respects per-tenant latency SLOs while optimizing GPU memory (KV cache) utilization and maintaining overall throughput. The allocator should enable graceful interruption (pause/resume), selective KV demotion/eviction, and short-term memory compaction windows, guided by predicted token budgets and latency envelopes. It must integrate with the existing continuous batching runtime and provide observability (why a slice was preempted/evicted) and a feedback loop for model-specific tuning.

acceptance_criteria:
New allocator integrated into continuous-batcher feature-flag and can be toggled per node
p95 latency for SLO-tagged tenants remains within 5% of target under 2x baseline load in 90% of test runs
KV cache churn reduced vs baseline by at least 12% for mixed workloads without increasing GPU OOM events
Preemption decisions logged with reason codes and correlated metrics (residency_score, predicted_tokens, memory_pressure)
Automation: rollout plan with canary on dedicated test pool and automated rollback if latency regressions detected

implementation_notes:
High-level plan:
1) Data model: compute a per-slice 'residency_score' = weighted function(resident_age, access_freq, recent_hit_rate) and a 'preempt_priority' combining SLO_urgency, predicted_remaining_tokens, and residency_score.
2) Eviction policy: implement two-tier demotion - soft-demote (move KV rows to on-device compressed slab) and hard-evict (drop to host or free) depending on predicted latency risk and memory headroom.
3) Interruption semantics: add pause checkpoint for model KV state and resumable execution with backoff windows to avoid thrashing.
4) Memory compaction: trigger short cooperative GC/compaction windows during low-latency slack identified by runtime telemetry.
5) Feedback loop: online estimator for token budget per tenant using rolling-window ML predictor; expose tuning knobs via config and console.
6) Observability: emit preempt_reason tags, residency_score, and expected_reclaim bytes to tracing and per-tenant dashboards.

Trade-offs discussed: strong SLO prioritization reduces throughput for batchy tenants — provide policy knobs (aggressive, balanced, economic) to let customers tune. Soft-demote reduces latency risk but increases token cost due to recompute on resume.

Integration points & PRs:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/continuous-batcher/eviction-allocator (internal)
- RFC: https://drive.redwood.ai/rfc/dynamic-allocator-v1.pdf
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

tasks:
Prototype residency_score computation in simulator
Add preempt_priority field to slice metadata and wire through admission path
Implement soft-demote and hard-evict code paths in KV manager
Build pause/resume checkpoint API and test model replay correctness
Add telemetry + tracing for preempt decisions
Run mixed-workload benchmarks and update canary runbooks

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Thrash between pause/resume if eviction oscillates under bursty traffic. Mitigation: hysteresis via backoff windows and token-budget prediction; observe via new metrics.
Risk: Increased token cost for resumed slices that need KV recomputation. Mitigation: surface 'economic' policy that favors cost; provide per-customer default policy and console override.
Risk: Unintended OOMs from compaction delays. Mitigation: conservative compaction thresholds and safety-kill fallback which logs and signals SRE runbook.

qa_plan:
Unit tests for residency score math, integration tests for pause/resume correctness across small LM and chat model, stress tests with mixed tenant SLAs (p50/p95/p99) run in perf-sims job, canary run in dedicated test pool with 48h monitoring and automatic rollback if p95 regresses >10% or error rate increases >0.5%
